title: Dataset Cards
goals: Inspect row meaning missing values and repeated records
Document dataset source schema and limitations
Separate observed quality flags from justified corrections
vocabulary: Where data came from and how it was created
The stated meaning types units and rules for fields
An unknown or unavailable value rather than a measured zero
A concise record of dataset contents creation intended use and limitations

worked_example.title: Write a card another person can use

blocks.text: For Robot practice v1, record the purpose as practising inspection, the source as teacher-authored fictional data, and the row meaning as an intended single indoor trip. Record the five-row count, the ID field, minutes as the duration unit and None as unknown. List the duplicate-ID and invalid-duration findings. State that no cleaning has occurred, no train/test split is assigned, and no model has been evaluated.

Add intended use, excluded uses, known gaps, version and a contact or owner. Here the lesson teacher maintains the practice copy; its allowed classroom purpose is inspection practice. Do not describe it as validated navigation data. For a real external dataset, also verify its actual permission or licence and collection context; an absent field in the documentation is an unanswered question, not permission to invent a value.

blocks.label: What fraction of the five raw rows has unknown duration? Can you subtract two missing rows, one negative row and one extra ID occurrence from five to count distinct usable trips? Explain using the B rows.

guided_practice.title: Interpret the audit counts
guided_practice.prompt: Explain each number in 5 4 2 1. How many extra ID occurrences are there, and how many rows belong to a repeated-ID group?
guided_practice.answer: The numbers mean 5 raw rows, 4 distinct IDs, 2 missing durations and 1 negative duration. There is 1 extra ID occurrence; 2 rows belong to the repeated-ID group B. These are different counts.

independent_case.title: Changed independent case
independent_case.task: Write key dataset-card entries for20 photos: five plants, four views each, one phone, one indoor setting. Growth labels have not been supplied.
independent_case.answer: Record collection source,20 images and five plant groups, view/device/setting coverage, missing label definitions, intended use and limitations. Specify a plant-group split and obtain a defensible label rule. Twenty images are not20 independent plants; no accuracy claim is supported without labels and evaluation.

misconceptions: A complete card certifies data quality
The card records evidence and gaps; its claims still need checking. Documentation does not prove suitability.
None is unknown; zero is a specific allowed value in this exercise. Substitution without evidence changes the meaning.
Flag counts can always be added
The same row can have multiple flags. Count rows or unique events under an explicit policy and retain the raw denominator.

Input → Model → Evidence
Trace the information, fitted behavior, and evaluation proof separately.
QUESTION  Complete a dataset card and identify two uses the data cannot support.
MODEL IDEA  A dataset card records where data came from, why it exists, its fields, collection process, known gaps, risks, and prohibited uses.
PROOF NEEDED  Use an unseen case, visible calculation, error analysis, and a stated limitation.
UNDER THE HOOD  Source: student-collected classroom plant photos with permission. Purpose: teach a low-stakes healthy-versus-spotted classifier.

A closer explanation

blocks.title: Python 3 code
blocks.text:
rows = [("A", 8), ("B", None), ("B", None),
        ("C", -2), ("D", 12)]
ids = set()
missing = 0
negative = 0
for trip_id, minutes in rows:
    ids.add(trip_id)
    if minutes is None:
        missing = missing + 1
    elif minutes < 0:
        negative = negative + 1
print(len(rows), len(ids), missing, negative)

A set stores each distinct ID once. The output is 5 4 2 1: five rows, four distinct IDs, two rows with unknown duration and one row with a negative duration. There is one extra occurrence beyond the four distinct IDs. This is not a count of all rows in repeated-ID groups: both B rows belong to that group.

blocks.title: Turn an observation into a documented action
blocks.caption: Flags can overlap: both rows with ID B also have missing duration. Do not add flag counts as if they were separate groups.

blocks.text: The code assumes every row is a pair and each duration is a number or None. It is a small audit, not full schema validation. It does not check text values, units, source truth or whether IDs refer to real unique events. A successful run does not certify data quality.

EVALUATION DESIGN
Four Tests, Four Kinds of Evidence
A system is not understood until it survives more than one comfortable example.
NORMAL  Expected data and expected behavior.
BOUNDARY  Value close to a threshold, ambiguous label, or uncertain prediction.
MISSING  Necessary field, label, source, or measurement is unavailable.
SHIFTED  New lighting, species, device, subgroup, or time condition.
RELEASE RULE  Passing one case never proves generalization. Predefine expected behavior for all four categories.
